Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — HelioCare is excited about Redwood's latency profile for private deployment. Legal has a few substantive asks on the DPA and SCC approach before procurement can proceed. I've attached our latest redline (HelioCare_DPA_redline_v3.docx) and an SCCs matrix that shows our transfer routes.

Two things we need clarified:
- Passporting: we currently ask for an explicit "passporting" clause in the Order Form so that we can restrict onward transfers to EU-only routes unless we approve otherwise. Is that something Redwood can contractually commit to (and how would that sit with your hosting / Dedicated pools)?
- TIA / fallback: our privacy team wants a short transfer-impact addendum (TIA) that lists the fallback routing if SCCs cannot be relied on for a subprocessor. We'd like Redwood to confirm the TIA approach rather than broad, open-ended delegation.

Timeline: procurement would like executed DPA + Order Form in ~3 weeks. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the passporting language or whether we need alternative mitigations (e.g., contractually documented hosting constraints + KMS controls)?

Laura / Ben — forwarding HelioCare’s redlines. TL;DR: they want an explicit passporting commitment in the Order Form + a short TIA enumerating fallback routing if SCCs are not adequate for a subprocessor. Procurement asks for signature in ~3 weeks.

My read: passporting will be operationally constraining if they want EU-only routes guaranteed; it could push them toward a Private or Dedicated-only solution or require firm subprocessor routing restrictions. We should propose two commercial/legal tracks:
  1) Option A: Tight passporting (Order Form clause + technical hosting constraints) — likely requires Dedicated/VPC or explicit region-lock; could carry a surcharge.
  2) Option B: SCCs + documented TIA and a commitments table (list of subprocessors + fallback policy) — more standard and lower friction.

Can Compliance produce a quick SCCs gap table and Legal a redline response? If Option A is viable, Sales (Ben) should confirm pricing impact and whether Dedicated pool reservation is acceptable.

I can join a call with HelioCare next week; if we respond with a clear option A/B outline and a proposed redline, should be enough to keep procurement on schedule.

Thanks — Karthik

(Attachment: original HelioCare materials)

Karthik / Ben — quick legal note after an initial pass. See attached: RWI_DPA_response_redline.docx (track changes) and SCCs_gap_table.csv (high level).

Summary / suggested approach:
- Passporting clause: we can accept a narrow, Order-Form-scoped passporting commitment that constrains onward transfers to specified regions/subprocessors identified in an annex. We cannot commit to an absolute global prohibition on transfers without explicit hosting constraints (Dedicated or Private).
- TIA (Transfer Impact Addendum): we propose a 2-section TIA: (1) routing fallback hierarchy (EU-hosted -> EU-subprocessor -> restricted transfer with supplementary measures) and (2) remedial covenant (notification + mitigation windows). Draft language included in our redline.
- Subprocessor list / evidence: Compliance will require the subprocessor list and KMS boundary description; we flagged the biggest gaps in SCCs_gap_table.csv.

Options for Sales to present:
A) Passporting + dedicated-hosting commitment: Customer gets annexed list + region lock. Requires a Dedicated commitment or Private deployment; pricing uplift to be discussed with Ben.
B) Standard SCCs + TIA: operationally simpler; we provide contractual TIA and enhanced audit rights; no hosting change. This is our recommended low-friction path unless the customer insists on strict passporting.

Action items:
- Legal (Laura): finish redline and prepare short summary of changes for external.
- Compliance (cc Ben for ops): validate SCCs_gap_table and prepare evidence list.
- Sales (Ben): confirm whether pricing uplift for Dedicated/VPC is an option and draft a quick commercial note if so.

I can review final draft before we send.

Ellie — thanks for the redlines and for the clarity on timeline. Looping Laura and Ben on our suggested approach.

Short version for procurement: we can offer two contract tracks. Please confirm which you prefer and we'll send the corresponding redline:

Option A (passporting + hosting commitment) — Redwood will include a passporting annex restricting onward transfers to the EU unless HelioCare gives prior written consent. To operationalize this we ask that the Order Form specify the deployment type (Dedicated or Private). Option A requires pricing discussion (Ben) and an explicit subprocessor annex; lead time for Dedicated provisioning is ~4–6 weeks.

Option B (SCCs + TIA; recommended) — Redwood accepts SCCs and adds a short Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA) that sets a fallback routing hierarchy and notification/mitigation steps. This path does not require infrastructure changes and should allow execution within your 3-week window.

Attachments: we’ve prepared RWI_DPA_response_redline.docx and an SCCs gap table (attached). For momentum, if you confirm Option B we’ll send the redline for signature and include a DocuSign envelope for the DPA + Order Form addendum: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/12345-helio-dpa

Can we schedule a 30-minute call Wednesday to walk the options? If Option A is preferred, Ben will run pricing and I can connect your procurement with our Dedicated team.
